questions.q: Why does an effective test-generation prompt include the transformation's spec, not just the code?
options: A code-only prompt just re-derives what the code already does, while a spec lets the LLM check whether the code actually satisfies the intended rules
The spec is required by the LLM's API and has no effect on test quality
Code-only prompts always produce more thorough tests
Specs are only useful for documentation, never for testing
questions.explain: A weak, code-only prompt re-derives the function's own behavior; a spec-driven prompt can catch cases where the code doesn't match what it's supposed to do.

questions.q: What is an LLM reliably good at when drafting test cases from a schema?
options: Systematically walking a type's boundary values, like 0, 100, negative numbers, and nulls
Knowing which customer IDs are internal test accounts
Predicting seasonal volume spikes in production data
Detecting that a legacy source sends dates as Unix epochs
questions.explain: Coverage breadth across a type's boundaries is exactly the mechanical, exhaustive work an LLM does well.

questions.q: Why would an LLM's draft test list stay silent about a legacy source system sending dates as Unix epoch integers?
options: The LLM only knows what's in the spec and context you gave it, and that quirk lives in the engineer's head, not the schema
LLMs cannot generate any tests involving dates
Unix epoch dates are impossible to test for
The LLM always assumes every source system behaves identically
questions.explain: Business-specific, undocumented edge cases aren't in any schema, so an LLM's draft won't cover them unless you feed the context in yourself.

questions.q: What is the correct workflow for using AI-generated test cases, per this lesson?
options: Draft with the LLM, review each case against real system behavior, trim what isn't real, then run the survivors as part of the actual suite
Run every AI-generated test immediately without review
Only use AI-generated tests, and delete any human-written ones
Skip drafting and have the LLM run the tests itself in production
questions.explain: Every AI-generated test list should be treated as a draft outline that a human reviews and trims before anything is run.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does an AI-generated test list represent before human review?
options: A draft outline, not a finished test suite
A finished, production-ready suite that needs no changes
A legally binding test contract
A replacement for the transformation spec itself
questions.explain: Treating the draft as final skips the review step that catches undocumented, business-specific edge cases.
